subject: ela

sections.scope_note: Arizona standards deferred. This crosswalk covers Florida B.E.S.T. ELA (2025), Grade 6, and IB MYP language and literature only. Rows are suggested (Label C). No ELA.6.F or ELA.6.C.1.1 exists in the Florida grade-6 file.

rows.topic_domain: Literary text - plot, theme, narrators, and poetic form
ib_framework_elements: MYP language and literature: criterion A Analysing
MYP global context: personal and cultural expression
rows.key_differences: Florida asks how character interaction develops a plot, how theme develops, how narrators or point of view shift, and how poetic forms (the clarification names sonnet and villanelle) affect meaning and style. MYP analysing is broader and does not name those forms.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: In a language and literature inquiry, analyse one scene for how two characters change the plot and how the narrator’s point of view shapes that scene.

rows.topic_domain: Informational text - sections, central idea, purpose, and argument
ib_framework_elements: MYP language and literature: criterion A Analysing
rows.key_differences: Florida asks how sections or features convey meaning, how a central idea develops, how authors’ purposes differ across accounts, and how an argument’s reasoning develops. MYP frames this as inquiry into texts, not that sequence.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Use two accounts from the class inquiry. Name the central idea of one and the type of reasoning in the other.

rows.topic_domain: Across genres - figurative language, paraphrase, time periods, and rhetorical appeals
ib_framework_elements: MYP language and literature: six skill areas include reading and viewing
rows.key_differences: Florida asks how figurative language contributes to tone, requires paraphrase rather than summary, compares authors from named literary periods, and asks students to identify rhetorical appeals. The public MYP pages do not list those periods or logos, ethos, and pathos.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Paraphrase a short non-literary text, then say which appeal (logos, ethos, or pathos) the class can point to in one sentence.

rows.topic_domain: Writing - narratives, claims, and expository texts
ib_framework_elements: MYP language and literature: criterion C Producing text
MYP global context: personal and cultural expression
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies narrative techniques and figurative language, a claim with logical reasoning and varied transitions, multi-source expository structure, and revision with adult and peer feedback. There is no ELA.6.C.1.1 in this grade. MYP producing text does not set those product rules.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Produce one narrative, claim, or explanation for an inquiry audience, then revise it using one piece of peer feedback.

ib_framework_elements: MYP language and literature: speaking and presenting
rows.key_differences: Florida requires a logical sequence, nonverbal cues, volume, pronunciation, and pacing. Public ATL text names communication skills without those delivery details.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Present one inquiry finding aloud in a planned order. A partner notes whether the pace matches the punctuation.

ib_framework_elements: MYP language and literature: criterion D Using language
rows.key_differences: The Florida benchmark is grade-level grammar, punctuation, capitalization, and spelling. The clarification lists verbals, adjective forms, and pronoun case. Those skills are not on the public MYP pages. Criterion D is only a title here; its 1-8 descriptors were not copied.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Edit the inquiry writing for the conventions the class has been taught, without treating that list as an MYP criterion.

rows.key_differences: Florida requires multiple reliable and valid sources, refocusing the inquiry, diverse digital media, and digital tools to produce writing. MYP research skills are broader and do not set that reliability rule.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Answer one inquiry question from at least two sources the class judges reliable, and add one digital element that adds information rather than restating it.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies academic vocabulary, Greek and Latin roots and affixes, and connotative as well as denotative meaning. The public MYP pages do not list those strategies.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Choose a few inquiry words, test one meaning with a root or affix, and use the word in speaking or writing.

version_notes: 2026-10-03: Grade 6 FL↔IB crosswalk for MYP, not PYP. Arizona left empty (deferred). Rows are suggested alignments (Label C). Florida IDs are from the grade 6 drafts. IB elements are public MYP framework text or criterion titles from the linked subject brief. No IB learning outcomes and no 1-8 criterion descriptors were invented.
